newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe comments on new shareholder suit.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe comments on new shareholder suit.

text.p: CompuServe Corp said a shareholder lawsuit filed this week by the board that manages Florida's $55 billion pension fund did "not in any substantive way add to the securities claims already pending" against the company.
Another shareholder suit was filed last summer in a federal court in Ohio as a class action.
"Presumably this shareholder was already encompassed within the class of shareholders envisioned by the litigation already pending," the company said in a statement, referring the Florida suit.
CompuServe said it thought all the litigation was without merit and that it would defend itself vigorously.

Attorneys for the Florida Board of Administration filed a suit this week in Franklin County Common Pleas Court in Columbus, where CompuServe is based. A lawyer said the board preferred a separate suit to joining the class action.
The new suit alleges CompuServe, in the prospectus for its April 1996 initial public offering, made "materially false and misleading statements" about its now-defunct WOW! service.
The pension fund bought 130,300 CompuServe shares for about $4.2 million in April. The IPO price was $30. The price at Thursday's close on the Nasdaq was 9-1/4.
The pension fund's suit seeks unspecified compensatory damages, interest, costs and expenses.
CompuServe, with five million subscribers, including those in a Japan franchise, is the second-largest provider of computer online services. America Online Inc has about eight million.
CompuServe is 80 percent owned by tax preparation firm H&R Block Inc.
